head: ed22d6b
pattern_this_round_exposed: A distinct pattern from the one tracked in rounds 1-2, and quieter. Rounds 1-2's failure was a repair INTRODUCING a new defect. R12 and R13 are a repair being PARTIAL — the finding is closed, the artifact says `fixed`, the gate stays green, and the falsified claim goes on living at every site the sweep missed. A partial repair is externally indistinguishable from a complete one.
why_partial_repairs_hide: The fix site and the finding site are the same place, so the repair always looks complete from where you are standing. Grep-first/grep-after works because it moves the completeness question off the diff and onto the tree. That is a method, not an observation, and the next person to close a finding in this repo should meet it.

resolutions.detail: Swept by grep rather than at the sites the finding named. The falsified origin-arithmetic justification was published at SEVEN sites in total; five survived the R10 repair and are now corrected, including specs/decisions/INDEX.md's ADR-035 digest and the code comments at both `vision[0]` assignment sites. The site count IS the finding: R10 corrected two of seven and read as complete.
resolutions.declared_survivors: planner.py's TOOL_TABLE and agent.py:1044 keep their wording deliberately. The distinction: those two are MODEL-FACING GUIDANCE — text the model reads to choose an action — not published rationale a human reads to understand why the rule exists. A guidance string that says a coordinate from an element crop is untrustworthy is true and useful to the model regardless of which argument grounds the rule. Published rationale must be true; guidance must be actionable.
resolutions.sweep_blind_spot_disclosed: planner.py:408 escaped the first regex only because the phrase is split across concatenated string literals — not because it was absent. Recorded because a grep result reported without its blind spots is a weaker claim than the same result reported with them.

resolutions.detail: All three neighbouring clauses re-derived from the committed ledger rather than re-typed. The CONCLUSION — case-count growth, not per-case cost — was correct throughout and is untouched; only its numbers were wrong. Residual class filed as M43-D7 (below) rather than swept.

ADR-029's `Amended by` line to ADR-035 added. Worth one clause of its own: ADR-029's `Amends` line already records PR #57 R25 finding exactly this omission in ADR-021, so the file did to its successor precisely what its predecessor had done to it, and documented the defect in the same breath. That recursion is a stronger argument for grading the link than any assertion could be.

The degenerate shape is now described as one that COVERS the viewport in both axes, not merely 'at least as large as' it — matching M43-D6's repro, which had it right while the prose beside it did not.

The one-directional ceiling is stated in the same sentence that declares the grader authoritative: the strict inequality catches an element frame that is secretly a viewport shot, and nothing catches a viewport frame that is secretly a crop. Widening `_shot_ok`'s viewport branch is a grader change this round is not making.

debt_logged_this_round.detail: Wall-clock figures published OUTSIDE the graded band bullets are read by no grader: `published-band-matches-the-ledger` reads the Band-source bullet and nothing else, so a figure quoted in a narrative paragraph can contradict the ledger committed beside it and stay green forever. R13 is the demonstrated instance, found because a reviewer read the paragraph rather than because anything failed. The block deliberately does NOT run the sweep — recording the class is a finding; running the grep would be widening the implementation that produced it.

gate.note: orchestrator re-measures independently before the round is closed
